core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 4335-4352): let y' -> y over B' inside B be a minimal object of the category of morphisms to y, and let x' -> x be its image under f_*; if (x'' -> x) -> (x' -> x) is a morphism with x'' over A'' inside f(B'), then (S1) produces y'' -> y' over the fibre product B' x_{f(B')} A'', and minimality of y' forces that fibre product to be isomorphic to B', hence A'' = f(B'), so x' -> x is minimal.

Part (2) (proof lines 4354-4369): suppose f : B -> A is surjective and y -> x lies over f; given a minimal object x' -> x over A' inside A, (S1) produces y' -> y over the preimage B' = f^{-1}(A') whose image under f_* is x' -> x; choosing a minimal object y'' -> y dominated by y' -> y, its image under f_* maps to x' -> x, hence is isomorphic to it by minimality of x' -> x.
Conclusion (proof lines 4369-4371): the two statements together say that minimality is preserved by f_* and that every minimal object of the target arises this way, which is the assertion.
proof_roadmap: Reduce a competing morphism in the target category to the source using (S1).
Use minimality of the chosen object in the source to force the comparison ring map to be an isomorphism.
In the other direction lift along a surjection using (S1) and control the result by minimality.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves two statements about the functor taking a morphism into x to a morphism into y along a ring map: minimal objects go to minimal objects, and along a surjection every minimal object of the target category is the image of a minimal object of the source category (statement lines 4321-4333). The proof (proof lines 4335-4372) reduces competing morphisms in the target to the source using (S1) and forces the comparison to be an isomorphism by minimality, and in the other direction lifts along the surjection and controls the result by minimality. H2: two implications with three inputs, written out in full.
